children: AdaniConneX is in talks with domestic and international lenders for an offshore facility with a proposed tenure of five to seven years
Adani Group is seeking to raise around $1.5 billion through an offshore loan to finance its expansion into data centres, according to people familiar with the matter.

AdaniConneX Pvt., a joint venture between the Adani Group and data centre operator EdgeConneX, is in discussions with lenders including DBS Group Holdings, First Abu Dhabi Bank and Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group for the proposed facility, the people said.

The discussions also involve Natixis, ING Bank and Societe Generale, they added. Talks on pricing are under way, while the loan could have a tenure of five to seven years. The terms have not been finalised.
Adani Group plans to invest around $100 billion in data centres and other digital infrastructure by 2035, building on its existing energy business.
The expansion comes amid growing investment in India's data centre market, as companies seek to build computing capacity for artificial intelligence and cloud services.
Reliance Industries, led by Mukesh Ambani, has also outlined plans to invest up to $110 billion over seven years in artificial intelligence-related infrastructure.

India's data centre capacity is expected to increase to nearly 8 GW by 2030 from around 1.57 GW in August 2026, according to government estimates cited in local media reports. The sector could attract around $200 billion in investments over the next seven to eight years, the reports said.
